headline: An agent asked 9 standard buyer questions about Torch Technologies today. It could not answer 7 of them, and 5 hard-filter fields are missing entirely. Legibility score: 34.

dimensions.label: Discoverable
dimensions.question: Can an agent legally and technically reach this content?
dimensions.summary: 3 of the four major AI crawlers are blocked outright.

evidence.label: robots.txt served
evidence.detail: A robots.txt exists, so crawler policy is at least stated.

evidence.label: No blanket crawl block
evidence.detail: No site-wide Disallow. Crawlers can reach the content.

evidence.label: GPTBot posture
evidence.detail: GPTBot is explicitly blocked. Content from this site cannot be used by the assistant it feeds.

evidence.label: ClaudeBot posture
evidence.detail: ClaudeBot is explicitly blocked. Content from this site cannot be used by the assistant it feeds.

evidence.label: PerplexityBot posture
evidence.detail: PerplexityBot is unnamed. Access is implied rather than granted, and it changes whenever the CDN default changes.

evidence.label: Google-Extended posture
evidence.detail: Google-Extended is explicitly blocked. Content from this site cannot be used by the assistant it feeds.

evidence.label: Content-Signal policy
evidence.detail: Content-Signal is present (content-signal, search, ai-train) but does not address ai-input directly.

evidence.label: sitemap.xml
evidence.detail: Sitemap resolves with 142 URLs, giving crawlers a complete inventory.

evidence.label: Sitemap declared in robots.txt
evidence.detail: robots.txt points to the sitemap, which is how most crawlers find it.

evidence.label: llms.txt
evidence.detail: No llms.txt. There is no file on this domain written for a model rather than a browser, so every assistant reconstructs the company from marketing pages.

evidence.label: MCP descriptor
evidence.detail: No /.well-known/mcp.json. Agents can read this company but cannot transact with it.

evidence.label: Homepage indexable
evidence.detail: The homepage is indexable.

evidence.label: HTTPS preserved end to end
evidence.detail: A request to https://torchtechnologies.com lands on http://www.torchtechnologies.com/. Agents and crawlers treat a downgrade to plain HTTP as a trust signal, and some refuse the fetch outright.

dimensions.label: Parseable
dimensions.question: Once an agent has the page, can it extract facts from it?
dimensions.summary: No structured data at all — every fact must be inferred from prose.

evidence.label: JSON-LD structured data
evidence.detail: No JSON-LD anywhere. Every fact about this company — name, address, services, hours — has to be inferred from prose.

evidence.label: Organization schema
evidence.detail: No Organization schema. There is no machine-readable statement of who this company is.

evidence.label: Service or Offer schema
evidence.detail: Services exist only as headings and paragraphs. Nothing is comparable field-by-field.

evidence.label: FAQ schema
evidence.detail: No FAQPage schema. Buyer questions are answered, if at all, in unmarked prose.

evidence.label: Structured data parses cleanly
evidence.detail: Nothing to parse.

evidence.label: Semantic landmarks
evidence.detail: 4 of 4 landmark elements (main, header, footer, nav) present. Landmarks tell a parser which text is content and which is chrome.

evidence.label: Single H1
evidence.detail: Exactly one H1 states the page's subject.
evidence.quote:
Torch Technologies is
Lighting the Pathway of Freedom

evidence.label: Heading hierarchy
evidence.detail: 8 headings form a clean outline.

evidence.label: Title and meta description
evidence.detail: Missing or thin: meta description.
evidence.quote: Torch Technologies - Lighting the Pathway of Freedom

evidence.label: Content present without JavaScript
evidence.detail: 7,104 characters of text are in the served HTML. Agents that do not run a browser still read the page.

evidence.label: Critical information outside PDFs
evidence.detail: No capability statements or rate sheets are locked in PDFs.

evidence.label: Images carry alt text
evidence.detail: 4 of 31 homepage images have no alt text. Anything stated only inside an image is unreadable.

evidence.label: Language declared
evidence.detail: Document language declared as "en".

evidence.label: Structured elements used
evidence.detail: 9 list or table elements. Lists and tables are the cheapest structure a page can carry.

dimensions.label: Priced
dimensions.question: Can an agent determine what working with this company costs?
dimensions.summary: Cost is entirely unknowable without contacting a human.

evidence.label: Pricing page exists
evidence.detail: No pricing page. An agent comparing vendors has nothing to put in the cost column.

evidence.label: Numeric prices published
evidence.detail: No dollar figures anywhere on the site. Cost is unknowable without a human conversation.

evidence.label: Units and tiers stated
evidence.detail: No units, tiers, or 'starting at' language. Any number present cannot be normalized against a competitor.

evidence.label: No pure contact-gate
evidence.detail: Pricing is gated behind a contact request with no figures published. To an agent this reads as 'unknown', and unknown loses to a competitor who published a range.
evidence.quote: …conducts regular in-progress reviews to ensure the final design will meet expectations. NEED HELP? LET'S TALK As one of the nation's top 100 defense companies, the services and solutions we provide directly su…

evidence.label: Contract types stated
evidence.detail: No mention of FFP, T&M, CPFF, or IDIQ. In GovCon these are the pricing model, and stating them is the honest substitute for a price tag.

evidence.label: Rate schedule discoverable
evidence.detail: No labor rates or GSA price list referenced. A contracting officer's agent cannot estimate cost from this site.

evidence.label: Market note
evidence.detail: Published list pricing is rare in defense services and its absence is not a failure of nerve. What is scored here is whether cost is knowable at all: rate schedules, contract types, and vehicle ceilings are the legible substitute.

dimensions.label: Comparable
dimensions.question: Can an agent place this firm side by side with a rival and see a difference?
dimensions.summary: Some specifics, but no explicit contrast with alternatives.

evidence.label: Explicit differentiator
evidence.detail: No sentence anywhere contrasts this firm with an alternative. An agent asked to compare has to invent the comparison.

evidence.label: Comparison page
evidence.detail: No comparison or alternatives page. The firm has no say in how it is described next to rivals.

evidence.label: Ideal-customer statement
evidence.detail: No statement of who this firm is for. Agents will include it in the wrong shortlists and exclude it from the right ones.

evidence.label: Capability copy is specific, not atmospheric
evidence.detail: Fog density is 14.6 weighted marketing phrases per 1,000 words. Above roughly 6, capability statements stop carrying comparable information.

evidence.label: Service taxonomy stated
evidence.detail: No NAICS codes. The firm's services are described only in its own words, in a market that procures by code.

dimensions.label: Current
dimensions.question: Can an agent tell whether any of this is still true?
dimensions.summary: Freshness signals are present and recent.

evidence.label: Copyright year current

evidence.label: Dated content within 12 months
evidence.detail: Most recent dated item is from 2026.

dimensions.label: Fog index
dimensions.question: Is the copy specific enough to carry information at all?
dimensions.summary: Dense marketing fog — the copy states very little.

evidence.label: Marketing-speak density
evidence.detail: 14.6 weighted stock phrases per 1,000 words across 3,561 words of site copy. Under 2 reads as a company describing itself; over 8 reads as a company describing nothing.
evidence.quote: Partnership leverages Oak Ridge National Laboratory capabilities and industry expertise to focus on rapid prototyping and scalable solutions for emerging…

evidence.label: No single dominant filler phrase
evidence.detail: "solutions" appears 21 times. A phrase repeated this often is the site's actual thesis, whether the company meant it to be or not.

evidence.label: Foggiest sentence is survivable
evidence.detail: At least one sentence is built almost entirely from stock phrases. This is the sentence a model will summarize the company with.
evidence.quote: Partnership leverages Oak Ridge National Laboratory capabilities and industry expertise to focus on rapid prototyping and scalable solutions for emerging…

signals.label: CAGE code
signals.why: The CAGE code is how a contracting system resolves a company name to an entity. Without it, an agent cannot confirm the firm it found is the firm in SAM.

signals.label: UEI (SAM Unique Entity ID)
signals.why: The UEI replaced DUNS as the federal identity key. It is the single field that makes a firm machine-resolvable across SAM, USAspending, and every prime's supplier portal.

signals.label: DUNS (legacy)
signals.why: Retired federally in 2022, but still requested by some primes and databases. Cheap to publish alongside the UEI.

signals.label: NAICS codes
signals.why: Every federal opportunity is filtered by NAICS before anything else. A firm that never states its codes cannot be matched to the solicitations it should be winning.

signals.label: Set-aside / socioeconomic status
signals.why: Set-aside status is a hard filter on a majority of small-business solicitations. Unstated status means the firm is excluded from the searches it would automatically win.

signals.label: Business size standard
signals.why: Primes building a subcontracting plan filter on size before capability. Stating it removes a round of email.

signals.label: CMMC status
signals.why: CMMC is becoming a gate on any contract touching CUI. An agent screening for 'CMMC Level 2' matches on the literal string or not at all.

signals.label: NIST SP 800-171 / DFARS 7012
signals.why: The compliance posture behind CMMC. Naming it, with an SPRS score, is the difference between 'claims compliance' and 'documented compliance'.

signals.label: Quality certifications (ISO / AS9100 / CMMI)
signals.quote: …tal obligations, and continuously improving our Environmental Management System (EMS). Scope of our AS9100 Rev. D and ISO 14001:2015 Certifications Provide Engineering, Support Products,and Services to Gove…
signals.why: Quality registrations are checkbox filters in supplier qualification. They are trivially verifiable and their absence is read as absence, not as silence.

signals.label: Contract vehicles
signals.quote: …fs Leadership Locations Our History Quality Contact Us Contracts Consortium Membership D3I Domain 2 EXPRESS GSA OASIS GSA ASTRO GSA Schedules MDA TEAMS RS3 Solutions Advanced Technologies Cybersecurity & IT…
signals.why: A vehicle is a shortcut to award. An agent asked 'can we buy from them this quarter' is really asking which vehicle they are on.

signals.label: Past performance citations
signals.why: Past performance is the evidence layer of every proposal. If it exists only in a PDF or a proposal library, no agent can weigh it.

signals.label: Facility clearance / cleared staff
signals.why: Clearance level is a hard gate on classified work. Firms routinely hold an FCL and never mention it, and get filtered out of the exact work they are cleared for.

signals.label: Customer agencies named
signals.quote: …y Contact Us Contracts Consortium Membership D3I Domain 2 EXPRESS GSA OASIS GSA ASTRO GSA Schedules MDA TEAMS RS3 Solutions Advanced Technologies Cybersecurity & IT Engineering Technology Integration & P…
signals.why: Agency names are the vocabulary buyers search in. 'Federal customers' matches nothing; 'Missile Defense Agency' matches the query.

signals.label: Physical address stated
signals.value: 4090 Memorial Parkway SW | Building 1 Huntsville, AL 35802
signals.quote: …you for your interest in Torch Technologies. We are a 100% employee owned company headquartered in Huntsville, Alabama with employee owners located in Colorado, Florida, Hawaii, Maryland, Massachusetts, Michigan, New M…
signals.why: Geographic filters are the second most common after NAICS. 'Near Redstone Arsenal' is a literal proximity query an agent runs against a literal address.

signals.label: Teaming / subcontracting point of contact
signals.quote: …his communication about? Torch Accessibility Torch Capabilities Torch Engineering Torch Contract or Teaming Torch Public Affairs Selling to Torch General Questions Purchase Order Terms Name* Email* Phone Com…
signals.why: Primes looking for a teammate need a named route in. A generic contact form is where teaming inquiries go to die.

signals.label: Capability statement in HTML
signals.why: Nearly every firm has one as a PDF. Almost none publish it as a web page, which is the only form a retrieval pipeline can actually read.

govcon.verdict: Torch Technologies is missing 5 of the 6 fields an agent uses as hard filters: CAGE code, UEI (SAM Unique Entity ID), NAICS codes, Set-aside / socioeconomic status, CMMC status. Any query specifying one of these excludes the firm silently.
govcon.failedQuery: "Find me a [set-aside status] in Huntsville, Alabama with [CMMC level] under NAICS [code] for missile-defense software."

fixes.title: Add JSON-LD structured data sitewide
fixes.detail: Organization, Service, and FAQPage markup turn prose into fields. Without it, every fact about the company is a guess made by a parser.

fixes.title: Decide the Content-Signal policy deliberately
fixes.detail: The current ai-input directive tells assistants they may not ground answers in this content. That is usually a CDN default rather than a decision. Make it a decision.

fixes.title: Declare the company as an Organization entity
fixes.detail: Name, legal name, address, identifiers, sameAs links to SAM and LinkedIn. This is how a model stops treating the company as a webpage and starts treating it as a thing with attributes.

fixes.title: Publish an llms.txt
fixes.detail: A single machine-first file at the domain root stating what the company is, what it sells, who it serves, and where the authoritative pages live. It is the cheapest legibility gain available and takes under an hour.

fixes.title: State CAGE code on the site
fixes.detail: The CAGE code is how a contracting system resolves a company name to an entity. Without it, an agent cannot confirm the firm it found is the firm in SAM.

fixes.title: State NAICS codes on the site
fixes.detail: Every federal opportunity is filtered by NAICS before anything else. A firm that never states its codes cannot be matched to the solicitations it should be winning.

fixes.title: State Set-aside / socioeconomic status on the site
fixes.detail: Set-aside status is a hard filter on a majority of small-business solicitations. Unstated status means the firm is excluded from the searches it would automatically win.

fixes.title: State UEI (SAM Unique Entity ID) on the site
fixes.detail: The UEI replaced DUNS as the federal identity key. It is the single field that makes a firm machine-resolvable across SAM, USAspending, and every prime's supplier portal.

fixes.title: Unblock the AI crawlers you did not mean to block
fixes.detail: GPTBot, ClaudeBot, Google-Extended cannot read this site. Name every AI agent in robots.txt and decide each one on purpose.

fixes.title: Build a parseable pricing page
fixes.detail: Even without list prices: contract types, labor-category structure, typical engagement sizes, and vehicle ceilings. Something has to fill the cost column.

fixes.title: Give past performance a structured home
fixes.detail: One page, one entry per engagement: customer, scope, period, role (prime or sub), outcome. This is the single highest-value page most GovCon sites are missing.

fixes.title: Name the programs and platforms supported
fixes.detail: Within release constraints, name them. These are the literal strings buyers search on, and 'advanced defense systems' matches none of them.

fixes.title: Publish at least one real number
fixes.detail: A range, a starting point, or a published rate schedule. An agent comparing three vendors will rank the two with numbers above the one without, every time.

fixes.title: State CMMC status on the site
fixes.detail: CMMC is becoming a gate on any contract touching CUI. An agent screening for 'CMMC Level 2' matches on the literal string or not at all.

fixes.title: Mark up each service as a structured entity
fixes.detail: One Service node per capability, each with an area served and an audience, so a requirement can be matched field by field.

fixes.title: Publish a structured FAQ
fixes.detail: The buyer questions already arriving by email, answered on the page in FAQPage markup. This is the format answer engines quote most directly.

fixes.title: Put numbers on the claims
fixes.detail: Headcount, years in market, facility size, cleared staff, contract count. Numbers are the only claims a model can rank.

fixes.title: Replace the pricing contact-gate
fixes.detail: 'Contact us for pricing' reads to a model as 'unknown'. Keep the contact route, but put a range or a structure beside it.

fixes.title: State Business size standard on the site
fixes.detail: Primes building a subcontracting plan filter on size before capability. Stating it removes a round of email.

fixes.title: State one checkable difference
fixes.detail: A sentence that a competitor could not truthfully copy. Everything else on the site is table stakes.

fixes.title: Stop the HTTPS downgrade
fixes.detail: The canonical URL redirects to plain HTTP. Some crawlers refuse the fetch, and every one that accepts it discounts the source. This is a redirect rule, not a project.

fixes.title: Rewrite the foggiest copy
fixes.detail: Replace stock phrases with specifics: what was built, for whom, on what, with what result. Fog is the one defect that survives every redesign.

fixes.title: State Facility clearance / cleared staff on the site
fixes.detail: Clearance level is a hard gate on classified work. Firms routinely hold an FCL and never mention it, and get filtered out of the exact work they are cleared for.

fixes.title: State NIST SP 800-171 / DFARS 7012 on the site
fixes.detail: The compliance posture behind CMMC. Naming it, with an SPRS score, is the difference between 'claims compliance' and 'documented compliance'.

fixes.title: State Past performance citations on the site
fixes.detail: Past performance is the evidence layer of every proposal. If it exists only in a PDF or a proposal library, no agent can weigh it.

fixes.title: Write the comparison page yourself
fixes.detail: If the firm does not describe how it differs from the alternatives, a model will infer it — usually wrongly, and usually to the incumbent's benefit. An honest comparison page is a defensive asset.

fixes.title: Say who this is for, and who it is not for
fixes.detail: Explicit fit criteria let agents screen correctly in both directions, which raises lead quality more than it lowers lead volume.

fixes.title: State the contract types worked under
fixes.detail: FFP, T&M, CPFF, IDIQ. One line on the pricing page. In this market that line is the pricing model.

fixes.title: Attach a number to at least one result
fixes.detail: One measured outcome per case study. Cleared for release, approximate is fine — adjectives are not.

fixes.title: Expose an MCP endpoint for agents
fixes.detail: A /.well-known/mcp.json plus a small server lets an agent query capabilities, check availability, and open a teaming inquiry without a human in the loop. Almost no competitor has one.

fixes.title: Publish or link the labor rate schedule
fixes.detail: If a GSA price list exists, it is already public. Link it from the site rather than leaving it on GSA Advantage alone.

fixes.title: Caption the images
fixes.detail: Anything stated only inside an image does not exist to a text-based agent.

fixes.title: Emit accurate lastmod dates
fixes.detail: lastmod values that reflect real edits, so crawlers spend their budget on what changed.

fixes.title: Attribute the quotes
fixes.detail: A named person and organization behind each quote. Unattributed praise is discarded as noise.

notes: Every score is the ratio of points earned to points available across the checks listed under each dimension. No curve, no judgment call after the fact.
This audit reads the site the way a non-rendering agent does: fetch, parse, extract. No browser, no JavaScript execution.
